name: GATE Overflow CS Test Series 2026 | Quantitative Aptitude | Shallow Test 1

question.text:
The probability that it is Wednesday and an employee is late is 0.06. Since there are 5 working days in a week, the probability that it is Wednesday is 0.2. What is the probability that an employee is late given that today is Wednesday?
  1. 25%
  2. 20%
  3. 30%
  4. 15%
The sum of all the possible integer values of \( x \) in the equation \( |x + 5| + |x - 8| = 13 \) is _______

It has been found that the number of individuals in a certain population doubles every 10 days. If the current number of available resources is 80,000 and there are 10,000 individuals currently using these resources, in how many days will the resources be exhausted?
  1. 30
  2. 31
  3. 32
  4. 33

At 3:20, the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock form an angle of ________ degrees.
  1. \(20^\circ\)
  2. \(30^\circ\)
  3. \(40^\circ\)
  4. \(50^\circ\)

If \( ^{n}C_{3}, ^{n}C_{4} \), and \( ^{n}C_{5} \) are in A.P., then the possible values of \( n \) are ___________
  1. \(\dfrac{19 + \sqrt{41}}{2}, \dfrac{19 - \sqrt{41}}{2}\)
  2. \(\dfrac{17 + \sqrt{41}}{2}, \dfrac{17 - \sqrt{41}}{2}\)
  3. \(\dfrac{23 + \sqrt{41}}{2}, \dfrac{23 - \sqrt{41}}{2}\)
  4. \(\dfrac{25 + \sqrt{41}}{2}, \dfrac{25 - \sqrt{41}}{2}\)

When a two-digit number \( N \) is multiplied by the difference of its digits, the result is 128. When the number obtained by reversing the digits of \( N \) is multiplied by the difference of its digits, the result is 92. The sum of the digits of \( N \) is ________.

A. 7

B. 9

C. 10

D. 11

A cyclist traveling at \(\frac{4}{5}\) of his usual speed is 20 minutes late. What is the usual time taken in minutes by him to cover the same distance?
  1. 100
  2. 80
  3. 60
  4. 40

If the difference between the roots of the equation \( x^2 + bx + 4 = 0 \) is less than \( \sqrt{48} \), then the set of possible values of \( b \) is ________
  1. \((-10, 10)\)
  2. \((-8, 8)\)
  3. \((-8, 7)\)
  4. \([-7, 7]\)

A group of twelve friends decided to share equally the cost of a birthday gift for their friend. However, when four of them opted out of contributing, the remaining friends had to pay an additional Rs. 800 each to cover the cost of the gift. What was the total cost of the gift in rupees?

\( a, b, \) and \( c \) are three non-negative integers such that \( a + b + c = 24 \). The maximum value of \( ab + bc + ca + abc \) is _____.
  1. \( > 700 \) and \( \leq 750 \)
  2. \( > 800 \) and \( \leq 850 \)
  3. \( > 900 \) and \( \leq 950 \)
  4. \( > 950 \) and \( \leq 1000 \)

If the area of a square is increased by 69%, what will be the percentage increase in its perimeter?
  1. 15%
  2. 20%
  3. 30%
  4. 34%

One of the factors of \(7^{2k} + 4^{2k}\), where \(k\) is an odd number, is ______
  1. \(45\)
  2. \(77\)
  3. \(49\)
  4. \(65\)

What is Aryan's present age, if after 10 years his age will be 4 times his age 5 years back?
  1. 8  
  2. 12
  3. 10  
  4. 15

A project manager undertakes to complete a project in 180 days. He employs 400 workers for 60 days, and they complete half of the project. He then reduces the number of workers to 250, who work for 45 days, after which there are 20 days of holidays. How many workers must be employed for the remaining period to finish the project?
  1. 160
  2. 231
  3. 180
  4. 232

What is the remainder when \( (37)^{2022 \times 2021!} - 1 \) is divided by 5?
  1. 3
  2. 2
  3. 1
  4. 0

Two numbers in the base system \( B \) are \( 302 \) and \( 512 \). The difference of these two numbers in the decimal system is \( 210 \). The value of \( 3535 \) in the decimal system is ______.
  1. 3535
  2. 1795
  3. 1910
  4. 2055

The pie chart shows the amount of time each day that John spends on various activities. What is the angle in degrees for the sector of the pie chart representing the time he spends on Exercise (rounded to the nearest integer)?
Pie Chart:

  1. \(43^\circ\)
  2. \(72^\circ\)
  3. \(90^\circ\)
  4. \(60^\circ\)
If \( M = 5^{15} + 5^{30} + 5^{45} \), then how many distinct prime factors of \( M \) are there?

Consider the following data on Zebra Fever pandemic.
(K stands for Thousand, M for Million, and B for Billion)

\[
\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Country} & \text{Positive Cases} & \text{Fatality Rate (among infected)} & \text{Population} \\
\hline
\text{Brazil} & 210\text{K} & 8\% & 210\text{M} \\
\text{Canada} & 190\text{K} & 12\% & 38\text{M} \\
\text{Japan} & 240\text{K} & 7\% & 125\text{M} \\
\text{Mexico} & 150\text{K} & 9\% & 128\text{M} \\
\text{Russia} & 300\text{K} & 10\% & 146\text{M} \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]
If the accuracy of the tests and the number of positive cases per million tests are the same, which country would you rather be in if your aim is to survive your life from Zebra Fever?
  1. Brazil
  2. Canada
  3. Japan
  4. Mexico

The value of \(\left(\frac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)^{2025} \left(\frac{1 -i}{1 + i}\right)^{2023}\), where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\), is _______.
  1. \(1\)
  2. \(-1\)
  3. \(i\)
  4. \(-i\)

A sector has a radius 14 cm and angle \(45^\circ\). Its area equals ______

  1. 76.98 cm\(^2\)
  2. 77.56 cm\(^2\)
  3. 76.58 cm\(^2\)
  4. 77.42 cm\(^2\)

Evaluate the sum:
\[ \sum_{k=1}^{2023} i^k \]

=imaginary unit, $i=\sqrt{-1}$
  1. \(0\)
  2. \(1\)
  3. \(i\)
  4. \(-1\)

If a cyclist travels at 30 km/hr instead of 25 km/hr, he would have traveled 50 km more. What is the actual distance traveled by him?
  1. 150 km
  2. 250 km
  3. 300 km
  4. 200 km

The polynomial \( x^4 - ax^3 + bx^2 - cx + 4 \) when divided by \( x - 2 \) leaves a remainder of 5 and when divided by \( x + 2 \) leaves a remainder of 11. Then \( b^2 = \)____
  1. 25
  2. 36
  3. 9
  4. 4

Four partners shared the profit in a business in the ratio 8:6:4:3. They had partnered for 12 months, 8 months, 15 months, and 10 months respectively. What was the ratio of their investments?
  1. \(40:45:16:18\)
  2. \(20:15:12:9\)
  3. \(12:15:18:20\)
  4. \(50:40:30:25\)

The 2nd term of a G.P. is 18 and its 5th term is 486, then the common ratio of the G.P. is ________

  1. \( 2 \)
  2. \( 3 \)
  3. \( 4 \)
  4. \( 5 \)

The number of common terms in the two sequences: \( 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, \ldots, 1500 \) and \( 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, \ldots, 1400 \) is _________
  1. 40
  2. 20
  3. 42
  4. 35
